frontier.hypothesis: Directed permuter over PERM_STMT_LIST reorderings + PERM_ADD_SUB / PERM_DUMMY_COMMA_EXPR / PERM_REORDER_DECLS mutations finds a spelling that shifts sll's LUID above move16's WITHOUT (a) introducing a second tree-level a0<<4 (which triggers s6's local/global pool split) OR (b) source-ordering i=a0 before v1=a0<<4 in a straight-line block (which triggers s7's cse.c operand substitution).
frontier.mechanism: s6 and s7 pin two orthogonal pass-level dead ends for hand-derivation. Permuter can explore C shapes that route around BOTH — e.g. mutations that split blocks so cse.c doesn't see the i=a0 -> v1=a0<<4 sequence in one processing region, or that eliminate the second tree-level shift via non-obvious commutative/associative rewrites.

frontier.hypothesis: A C spelling that expresses `v1 = a0<<4` and `i = a0` across a control-flow join (rather than a straight-line block) prevents cse.c's basic-block-scoped value-numbering from seeing them as value-equivalent, breaking the CSE fold that shortens a0's live range in the rotation branch.
frontier.mechanism: cse.c's basic_block_extended_end / cse_extended_basic_block bounds value-numbering to a single processing region. Cross-block equivalences are established only at reload/global. If i=a0 lives in one block and v1=a0<<4 in a different block reachable from function entry (not a linear predecessor of i=a0), CSE cannot substitute at insn 17.
frontier.next_probe: Enumerate small C rewrites that keep the same semantics but split the prologue into two joinable blocks — e.g. an early-return-if-null guard that jumps around a trivial block containing v1=a0<<4, then falls through to the i=a0 assignment; or a conditional-move idiom. Verify each keeps the sandbox score close and doesn't add insns. Measure whether cse.c picks up the value-equivalence across the split.
